newsitem.title: HONG KONG: C.P. Pokphand to sell loss-making unit.
newsitem.headline: C.P. Pokphand to sell loss-making unit.

text.p: C.P. Pokphand Co Ltd said on Thursday it had agreed to sell 70 percent of its loss-making C.T. Progressive (Distribution) Ltd unit to Clearline Investments Ltd for an estimated US$47.01 million.

C.P. Pokphand said in a statement the principal assets of C.T. Progressive are the entire issued share capital of Ek Chor Distribution System Co Ltd and an associated shareholder loan of HK$570.6 million to Ek Chor.
It said it would assign 70 percent of the benefit of the shareholder loan to Clearline Investments, which will take over the management of the company.
The final price paid will depend on the outstanding dollar value of the loan when the sale is completed plus interest, and a company official said the estimated amount may or may not change.
Clearline is owned in equal shares by C.P. Pokphand's chairman Dhanin Chearavanont and president Sumet Jiaravanon.
C.T. Progressive operates retail stores in Hong Kong, and in Shanghai and Shenyang in China via Ek Chor and has operated at a loss since it commenced operations in 1994.
C.P. Pokphand said it expected the unit to continue making losses in 1996 and in the near term.

"In order to better utilise the company's resources in developing its core agri-industrial and other businesses, the board has decided to reduce the company's interest in retail operations," C.P. Pokphand said.
The proceeds from the sale will be used for general working capital, it said.
C.P. Pokphand is an investment holding company.
